findings.problem: setAway()'s own header comment says it is "the ONLY writer of an item's distance" and that "the count, the date line, the accessible name and the readout cannot drift apart". It updates .b-away, .b-date, the .b-grab aria-label and .b-stepRead — and never #b-edit-date, the one field the owner is looking at. Driven at 1440, owner-editing: at open the field reads "8 August 2026"; after three presses of +7 the readout below it reads "Saturday 29 August 2026 · in 44 days", the row reads "Sat 29 Aug", data-away is 44, and the field still reads "8 August 2026". Two controls 6px apart state two different dates, and the wrong one is the editable one. Then pressing Enter in that untouched field fires commitDate on the stale string and silently drags the moment back 21 days (measured: away 44 -> 23, undo bar "moved 21 days earlier"). Three deliberate presses of the primary gesture are destroyed by one keystroke in the field beside them; a blur after any focus of that field does the same. The same second-writer pattern sits on the horizon: wireOwner captures atRest = note.textContent once at wire time, place() rewrites .b-gapNote on every edit, and speak() restores the captured snapshot on scroll — measured at 1440, after moving the first moment to 8 August, scrolling down and back to the top repaints "Nothing is planned until 1 August.", a sentence that is now false.
findings.fix: In setAway(), after computing iso, add: var when = root.querySelector('#b-edit-date'); if (when) { when.value = F.fmt.medium(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.year(iso); when.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false'); } — the same two-line pattern already used for .b-stepRead on line 570, so the input becomes the fifth consumer of the one date rather than an independent source of truth. In wireOwner's speak() (render-b.js:1029), replace the captured `atRest` with a live read: var said = !top || top === rows[0] ? gapSentence(rows[0].getAttribute('data-date')) : ...  so both writers of .b-gapNote derive from the same accessor.

findings.element: render-b.js:688 `focus: function () { event.currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }` and undo() at render-b.js:532-542
findings.problem: event.currentTarget is null once dispatch has finished, so every stepper history entry stores a closure that throws. Driven: click +7, then press the visible Undo control — "Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'focus')" every time. Two consequences, both measured. paintUndo() disables the Undo button before the closure runs, so disabling the focused control drops focus to document.body (measured activeElement = BODY at both 390 and 1440). And because the throw happens before line 541, `window.scrollTo(0, top.at)` — written expressly so undo "used to restore the moment and leave them a screen away from it" cannot happen — never executes: at 390px, scrollY went 400 -> 793 on undo instead of back to 400. So the product's one reversibility surface annihilates place and focus on the single most frequent undo there is, which is the first class in the paid-for defect library. The behaviour gate's assertion at interaction-check.mjs:468 ("undo returns focus to the control that made the change") passes vacuously: it only exercises the Ctrl+Z path, where focus was already on .b-step and never had to be restored.
findings.fix: Capture the node, not the event. In step()'s click handler (render-b.js:677) add `var pressed = event.currentTarget;` as the first line, then change the remember() entry to `focus: function () { if (pressed && pressed.isConnected) pressed.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }`. Additionally wrap the call site so no future closure can strand the scroll restore: in undo() (line 540) change to `try { if (top.focus) top.focus(); } finally { if (typeof top.at === 'number') window.scrollTo(0, top.at); }`.

findings.element: [data-act="retry"] (render-b.js:1545); data-spacing (master.html body attr, render-core.js presets/controls); .b-switch (render-b.js:476, b.css:577-598)
findings.problem: Three things on this master present themselves as operable and are not. (1) loading-slow — the state whose whole subject is a failure — offers one action, "Try again". Nothing anywhere handles data-act="retry"; driven, clicking it changes nothing: state stays loading-slow, aria-busy stays "false", no live region speaks, focus parks on the dead button. The behaviour gate asserts only its existence (interaction-check.mjs:2202, `slow.way === 1`). The file itself declares the rule it is breaking: `inert()` exists at line 471 under "Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise". (2) data-spacing is one of the four named decisions: it is written into <body data-spacing="measured">, carried by all three presets, and published in the Design Console as a two-option control with a paragraph of help copy ("Even sets the same items at one rhythm. The honest cost of measured is holes."). Zero rules in b.css or shell.css and zero lines in render-b.js read it; driven, ?spacing=even renders byte-identical item tops. The console the founder shows people ships a dead knob. (3) .b-switch is a <span>, tabindex -1, no role, cursor:auto, carrying "Mara & Finn one of three" inside 1px solid var(--fore-16) / border-radius 6px / min-height 32px — the same border colour, radius and height band as .b-act, sitting 560px from three real buttons drawn identically. It reads as the project switcher and is nothing. Its text also concatenates without a separator ("Mara & Finnone of three"), as does the disclosure name ("Behind you3 moments", measured off the AX tree at 390).
findings.fix: Replace `act("Try again", ...)` at render-b.js:1545 with a wired button: attach a click handler on the loading-slow node that calls `go("loading")` and writes "Trying again." into a .b-live status; or, if a retry cannot be modelled in the lab, use `inert("Try again in a moment")` per the file's own rule. Either implement data-spacing (an `[data-spacing="even"] .b-measure` branch in place() that lays items at index*ROW instead of away*px) or delete it from master.html's body attribute, from all three presets and from __elevate.controls in render-core.js:246-251. Make .b-switch a real control or stop drawing it as one: drop `border`, `border-radius` and `min-height` from .b-switch (b.css:581-584) so it sets as plain text beside .b-where. Add explicit separators: in bar() render `[projectName, " ", h("span", ...)]` and in behindBlock()'s head render the count as `" " + past.length + " moments"`.

findings.element: shell.css:87-102 (--gap-hair … --gap-page); every `gap:` in b.css; inline style strings in render-b.js:729, 755, 786, 1345, 1519-1525
findings.problem: The nine-step space ladder is declared under a twelve-line comment naming the defect it fixed ("it drifted to twenty-six distinct values"). audit.mjs enforces it by grepping `margin|padding` in the built .css files only, so margins and paddings are almost fully tokenised and the enforcement stops there. The actual spacing mechanism on this surface is `gap` on flex and grid, and it is untouched: 26 gap declarations across b.css and shell.css, exactly one of which uses a token (`gap: var(--gap-tight)`), carrying twelve distinct values — 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 28, 32, 48, 56, 64 — of which seven (6, 10, 14, 18, 32, 48, 64) are not steps on the ladder. `gap: 10px` alone appears nine times. Below that sits a second unreadable layer: render-b.js writes spacing as inline style strings (`gap:6px` x3, `margin:0 0 10px -5px`, `margin-bottom:8px`, `margin-bottom:12px`, `margin:26px 0 0`, `margin-top:26px`, `margin-top:14px`), which the source check cannot see at all because it reads .css files. And the ladder carries a self-granted escape hatch — `if (space && !/off-ladder/.test(line))` — used five times in b.css. The count of distinct vertical-space values on the built master is back near where the comment says it started; it has only moved to the properties the gate does not read.
findings.fix: Extend the source ladder in audit.mjs to `(?:^|[\s;{])(?:margin|padding|gap|row-gap|column-gap)(?:-(?:top|right|bottom|left))?:` and drop the /off-ladder/ exemption, then fix what it reports: replace `gap: 10px` with var(--gap-snug) (12) or var(--gap-tight) (8) per site, `gap: 6px` with var(--gap-hair), `gap: 14px` with var(--gap-line), `gap: 18px` with var(--gap-item), `gap: 32px` with var(--gap-block), `gap: 48px` and `gap: 56px` with var(--gap-major), `gap: 64px` with var(--gap-page) or var(--gap-major). Move the five inline `style="display:grid;gap:6px"` blocks in render-b.js onto a `.b-editGroup` class in b.css, and the seven skeleton dimensions in states.loading onto `.b-skel[data-slot]` rules so they are gradeable source rather than strings.

findings.element: .b-undoAct and .b-undo kbd (b.css:832-844); @media (pointer: coarse) at b.css:1335-1338; b.css:1304-1322
findings.problem: audit.mjs only inspects visible elements, and .b-undo is `display:none` (data-empty="true") or `visibility:hidden` (inside .b-edit) in all twelve states it visits, so nothing about the product's one reversibility surface has ever been graded. Driven with it filled, two things fail the file's own declared rules. (a) Hit target: b.css:1332 says "Forty-four pixels is the floor for anything a thumb presses, and the file wrote that down and then applied it to one control", then lists five selectors — .b-act, .b-seg button, .b-step, .b-grab, .b-linkField — and omits .b-undoAct. Measured at 390x844 with pointer:coarse matching, the Undo button renders 51x28: the one control that takes a change back is 16px under the floor the same rule was written to enforce. (b) Letterfit: the round-6 fix at b.css:1304-1322 moved .b-date, .b-behindDate, .b-unit, .b-origin, .b-where and .b-keeper off the uppercase label register onto text-transform:none + var(--track-data), and left `.b-undo kbd` behind on var(--track-label). Measured: kbd renders Geist Mono 11px, text-transform none, letter-spacing 1.76px; .b-date renders Geist Mono 11px, text-transform none, letter-spacing 0.44px. That is one family, one size and one role (audit.mjs derives role="body" for both) at two letterfits — the exact `tracking` failure audit.mjs is built to catch, on the one element it structurally cannot reach. Visually it is a tracked-out sentence-case string, a letterfit that exists nowhere else in the product, on the keyboard hint for the primary safety net.
findings.fix: Add `.b-undoAct` to the coarse-pointer list at b.css:1336 so it reads `.b-act, .b-seg button, .b-step, .b-grab, .b-linkField, .b-undoAct { min-height: 44px; height: auto; }`. Change b.css:844 to `letter-spacing: var(--track-data)` so kbd joins the data register its neighbours were moved to. Then close the blind spot: in audit.mjs's per-state loop, add one interaction pass for owner-editing that clicks `.b-step[data-delta="1"]` before evaluating AUDIT, so the filled bar is inside the measured perimeter from now on.

biggestWin: The measure earns the direction outright. Every vertical position is daysFromToday x pixelsPerDay written by one function, so a fortnight is twice a week on screen at every scale — 18px/day for the owner, 14 on the sheet, 8 on paper, 2 going backwards — and the proportion between one gap and the next is identical at all four. Nothing is hand-placed, the rail is labelled at its origin, the ticks and figures stay on the true pixel while only the words are pushed clear, and the honest cost (a real hole where a fortnight of nothing sits) is left in rather than flattered away. Around it the plumbing is deeper than any lab I have graded: ink, tracking, leading, size, radii and motion all declared as named ladders with the defect each one was written to kill recorded in the comment, one fore/back ladder so the light-lock is nine lines rather than a parallel stylesheet, forced-colours mapped rather than opted out of, reduced motion honoured completely, word-safe clamping that is idempotent and re-runs on fonts.ready, and a print path that composes to one identical A4 at 1024 and 1440. The guest artifact — the phone screen the whole company is judged by — is genuinely finished: one tab stop, no dead controls, no h-scroll at any of the six widths, no trims, correct accessible names on every row. What stands between this and 9.5 is not taste and not composition. It is one build week on the owner's editing surface: resync the When field to setAway, fix the currentTarget closure so undo stops throwing and keeps place, wire or remove the three dead affordances, and pull gap into the space ladder. None of it requires a different decision; all of it is code that already knows what it should do and says so in its own comments.
